source: W3C MusicXML 4.0 Tutorial - The MIDI-Compatible Part
license_note: W3C document; short factual summary with attribution.

chunks.text: MusicXML has notation elements (how music is displayed or printed) and sound elements (the sonic realization used for MIDI playback). Sound elements are the minimum needed to produce a MIDI file from MusicXML.

attributes holds divisions (units per quarter note; one value per part at the start of the first measure, e.g. 24 allows triplets and sixteenths), key (fifths: negative for flats, plus mode major/minor), time (beats and beat-type) and transpose (chromatic required; diatonic and octave-change optional; a B-flat trumpet uses diatonic -1, chromatic -2).

A note has pitch (step A-G, alter, octave) or rest, duration as an integer number of divisions, optional tie and chord. Always write alter, even when the key signature implies the accidental. rest measure="yes" marks a whole-measure rest. A tie has type start or stop (stop before start when a note has both). chord marks a note sounding together with the previous one; if durations differ the longest comes first, otherwise use separate parts.

Parallel lines use backup and forward to move the time counter, organised either as layers or as voice 1 / voice 2. barline is used for playback only to mark repeats and endings; bar-style is graphic only.

The sound element carries tempo (quarter notes per minute) and dynamics (a percentage of forte velocity). Without a sound suggestion MusicXML assumes MIDI velocity 90 (about forte) and defines no default tempo. Grace notes and ornaments such as trills have sound attributes (for example steal-time and start-note) so they play back correctly.
